title: Huge mailbox makes Outlook slow
symptom: Outlook is very slow for a user with a very large mailbox
user_description: Outlook takes forever to open and freezes when I search. I keep every email since 2015, just in case. Is that the problem?

options.why: Old mail may be needed for records, and deleting it all is far more than needed.

options.text: Turn off cached mode for everyone in the company
options.why: Changes everyone's Outlook for one person's problem and can make others slower.
Loses her mail history and does not address the cause.

options.text: Check the mailbox size, archive old mail as the company policy allows, remove big old attachments, and limit how much mail Outlook keeps offline (for example 1 year)
options.why: Less mail stored on the PC makes Outlook faster, while archiving keeps older mail available when needed.

hints: Does all her old mail need to be on the PC?
What does company policy say about keeping email?
real_world_tip: The 'mail to keep offline' slider is in the account settings. Older mail stays on the server and can still be searched online.
